items.text: SEASON 11 · EPISODE 7 · DRAFT  The Brennock County EOC · the second storm · Maya, Kit (the county’s new second engineer), Fitz, Quino and Director Oduya · Level L6 · Mastery support (reference only — choose the tool and say why)  Maya has been on since six this morning. She knows the radio gateway better than anyone — which is exactly why she’s still here, and exactly why that’s the problem.  ⚑ RV-185: fatigue is shown as a risk the roster manages, never a virtue — not medical advice. RV-182: the roster is the director’s. Some choices run on a clock — and some depend on your loadout.

items.title: Hour Sixteen
items.stakes: The only engineer who knows the radio gateway is at hour sixteen of a twelve-hour roster — and has just made a mistake.
items.reward: A handover that leaves nothing in one head — and an engineer who goes home.

objectives.text: Decide what to do about the error
Decide how the room stops depending on one person

items.rumor: Going home is part of the job.

items.text: Act I — “Three minutes on the wrong talkgroup”

items.prompt: 22:03. Fitz spotted it: FIRE-OPS 1, not 2. Three minutes. Nobody hurt. What now?
unknown: Who else can run the gateway
timeout: Maya keeps going into hour seventeen.

hints.text: Whose decision is it that you stay — and what does she need to know?

options.label: Fix it quietly and carry on
options.result: Fixed. Nobody logs it. Nobody asks why.
options.consequence: Hides the error — and the sixteen hours behind it.

options.label: Fix it with Fitz watching, log it with the times, and tell Director Oduya you're at hour sixteen — and that's why
options.result: Oduya: “Then you're done at half past. Who's your relief?” Kit is already in the room.
options.consequence: Correct it in the open and give the roster's owner the real reason.

options.label: Blame the gateway's confusing screen
options.result: It is confusing. It wasn't the reason.
options.consequence: A true fact used to avoid the real one.

options.label: Keep going — the storm needs you
options.result: At 01:40 you mistype a frequency on the status board.
options.consequence: The storm needs someone who can still see straight.
options.fail: Working past the roster isn't yours to decide — and it's how the error happened (RV-185).

items.title: Three minutes on the wrong talkgroup.
items.body: One digit. FIRE-OPS 1 is fire's fireground channel — crews inside flooded buildings; FIRE-OPS 2 is their flood net. For three minutes public works' traffic talked over the fireground until Fitz heard it. Nobody was hurt. Maya has been on for sixteen hours of a twelve-hour roster. It's the exact mistake a roster exists to prevent.
items.label: Test: how long — and how far over?

items.title: 22:00:10 · ‘FIRE-OPS 1 ⇄ WORKS-FLOOD’
items.body: The EOC's radio log: ‘22:00:10 patch FIRE-OPS 1 ⇄ WORKS-FLOOD (M.) · 22:03:10 corrected to FIRE-OPS 2 (M., F. witness).’ One digit. Three minutes.

items.title: Named teams, fixed handovers
items.body: During the Apollo missions in the 1960s, flight controllers at the U.S. space agency's mission control in Houston worked in named teams — White, Black, Maroon — and handed the consoles to the next team on a schedule, with a formal briefing. Even on the hardest days of the hardest missions, the next team took over at the planned time. Nobody flew a spacecraft on hour twenty.

items.text: Act II — “The only one who knows”

items.title: The only one who knows.
items.body: Why did she stay? Because the gateway's patch procedure lives on page 31 of Maya's own notebook. Eleven steps, in her handwriting. Nobody else in the building could build the flood patch from scratch. She'd called it dedication. Kit, who has watched her build systems that don't need their builders, calls it what it is: a single point of failure with her name on it.
items.label: Test: how much cover does one person give — and what fixes it?

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #108 · AVERY'S LENS  Nobody is safer for working past the limit  Fatigue is a failure mode. Rosters, written handovers and more than one person who knows each system keep a long operation safe — not one tired expert.  At hour sixteen of a twelve-hour roster, the only engineer who knew the radio gateway patched fire's fireground channel to the wrong agency.

items.alt: The EOC radio desk; Kit holds out his hand for Maya's notebook; Maya, reluctant, holds it.

bubbles.text: You told me at the Wyndmere: a building that needs one person isn't finished.
Then this room isn't finished. Take the brief.

items.prompt: Last time I saw you this tired was the Wyndmere opening. You told me then that a building that needs one person isn't finished.

options.label: “Then this room isn't finished either. Take the brief. I'll finish it tomorrow — with you.”
options.reply: Deal. Go home. I've got the night.

options.label: “This is different.”
options.reply: It's exactly the same. You're just the one inside it this time.

options.label: “I'll go in an hour.”
options.reply: You'll go when the brief's signed. That's twenty-five minutes.

items.prompt: 22:10. Kit is here. How do you hand over?
items.risk: A night shift missing one thing you forgot to say.
timeout: Maya is still at the desk at midnight.

hints.text: What would catch the thing you forgot to tell him?

options.label: Hand over verbally on the way out
options.result: Kit remembers most of it. The 02:00 patch change isn't most of it.
options.consequence: A handover made of memory at hour sixteen.

options.label: Write the handover brief — situation, open patches, the gateway's state, the 02:00 change, hazards, who's who — read it aloud, walk the desk together, Kit repeats it back, both sign; then go home
options.result: Kit's read-back catches the 02:00 patch change you'd forgotten to say. It's added. Signed at 22:35. Home at 22:40.
options.consequence: Nothing left in one head; the read-back finds what writing missed.

options.label: Stay two more hours to show Kit the ropes
options.result: At midnight you're both tired and the ropes are still in your notebook.

options.label: Go home but stay on call for the gateway
options.result: The phone rings at 01:50 and 03:10. You aren't resting and the room still needs you.
options.consequence: Home isn't rest if the system still depends on you.

items.prompt: The morning after. How does the room stop depending on one engineer?
items.risk: The next long night depending on whoever knows most.
timeout: The notebook goes back in Maya's bag.

hints.text: Would the room be safe if you weren't in it?

items.note: Draft decision (DR-S11E07). Option B needs Team at LIMITED or better.

options.label: Hire another engineer exactly like Maya
options.result: Now two people keep it in their heads.

options.label: Write the gateway runbook; train Kit and a dispatcher on every shift pattern; the director enforces the roster — twelve hours on, ten off — with a written handover at every change
options.result: Runbook v1 by noon. Kit ran the 02:00 change from it, Fitz watching. The roster goes on the wall with Oduya's signature.
options.consequence: Knowledge out of one head, and a roster its owner keeps.

options.label: Maya writes the runbook; training ‘after the storm season’
options.result: It's written. Nobody has practised it.
options.consequence: The best you can do without the people to train — written, not yet shared.

options.label: Maya works shorter shifts and stays the only one who knows
options.result: Rested, and still the single point of failure.
options.consequence: Fixes her hours, not the system.

items.alt: The roster sheet as the director signed it: Maya 06:00–18:00, Kit and a trained dispatcher 18:00–06:00, a dashed line at 18:00 marked ‘written handover’; twelve on, ten off, two people who can run the gateway.
items.caption: The roster, kept.

items.title: ‘gateway: patch steps (mine)’
items.body: Maya's own notebook, page 31: ‘Gateway — patch steps (mine).’ Eleven numbered steps in her handwriting. The only copy of how the room's interagency voice path is built.

items.alt: The EOC at the evening shift change; Director Oduya holds the signed roster; Kit, rested, holds the gateway runbook.

bubbles.text: Twelve on, ten off. My signature, my roster. Nobody's a hero in my room.
And the gateway runbook. Maya's handwriting's in the margins, but it works without her.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Fatigue is a failure mode, not a test of character. Rosters exist to stop the errors tired people make; put a number on how far past the limit you are (% = hours ÷ roster × 100). Hand over in writing — read aloud, walked, repeated back, signed — then go home. And if only one person can run a system, the system is broken: write the runbook and train two more.
REFLECTION (optional)  · What would stop working if you took two weeks off tomorrow?
